question.text: A source and a detector move away from each other in absence of wind with a speed of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>20</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>, with respect to the ground. If the detector detects a frequency of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1800</mn><mo> </mo><mi>Hz</mi></math> of the sound coming from the source, then the original frequency of source considering the speed of sound in the air <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>340</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> will be _____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Hz</mi></math>.

solution.text:
The formula of apparent frequency in terms of velocity of the source and observer is, f′=fv−v0v+vs, now put the values which are given in the question, 

⇒1800=f340−20340+20⇒f=1800×360320 Hz⇒f=2025 Hz
